intended_object: The topology on the localisation A_s of a Huber-type ring A (with pair of definition (A₀, I)), given numerators T and denominator s, as in Wedhorn, Adic Spaces, Proposition/Definition 5.51. It is the non-archimedean ring topology in which D = A₀[T/s] is a ring of definition and I·D is an ideal of definition, so the images of (I·D)^n form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body is `RingSubgroupsBasis.topology`, Mathlib's standard way to build a ring topology from a filtration of additive subgroups. The filtration used is `locIdealImage P T s S n`, the image in S of Jⁿ, where:
- J = `Ideal.map (A₀ → D) I` is the ideal I·D;
- D = `locSubring` = `Algebra.adjoin A₀ {t/s : t ∈ T}`, i.e. A₀[T/s].

This is exactly Wedhorn's construction: the topology on A_s with neighbourhood basis of zero {image of Iⁿ·D}.

The hypothesis `HasDenominatorPower` (some Iᴺ satisfies Iᴺ/s ⊆ D) is what makes left multiplication by 1/s continuous, which the basis needs. Wedhorn's hypothesis (T finite with T·A open) implies it, as the library proves in `hasDenominatorPower_of_isOpen_span`. So the definition is a mild generalisation of the textbook one (arbitrary T, and only separately continuous multiplication on A), not a restriction. On those inputs it agrees with Wedhorn's topology.

Taking S to be any `IsLocalization.Away s S`, rather than the concrete `Localization.Away s`, is also more general. Mathlib has no Huber rings or rational localisations, so there is no counterpart to cite.
